recipes.name: Pepperoni Rolls
ingredients_raw: 1 cup warm water (100 degrees F/40 degrees C)

steps.text: Stir together 1 cup warm water and 1/2 teaspoon sugar in a small bowl until sugar dissolves. Sprinkle yeast over water; let stand for 5 minutes.

Mix flour, 3/4 cup sugar, and salt in a large bowl. Stir in yeast mixture, beaten eggs, and melted butter until dough comes together. Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic, about 8 minutes.
Place dough into a greased bowl and turn to coat with oil. Cover with a light cloth; let rise in a warm place until doubled in volume, about 1 1/2 hours.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a cookie sheet.
Punch down dough; divide into 20 equal pieces about the size of a golf ball. Using your hands, flatten each piece into a small rectangle, about 4 inches square.

Place 3 overlapping slices of pepperoni down the center of each dough square. Place another row of 3 pepperoni slices next to the first. Roll dough around pepperoni, pinch the edges closed, and place rolls on the prepared cookie sheet.
Bake rolls in the preheated oven until bottoms are lightly browned and tops are barely golden, 14 to 16 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Pepperoni Rolls
raw_recipe.description: These pepperoni rolls are made with a homemade sweet, soft dough filled with savory pepperoni slices for a satisfying snack or quick and easy dinner.

review.reviewBody:
Wow - this along with Heavenly Hot Dog sauce are West Virginia originals that I'm going to start making here in Canada where I now live.

Watch out Canadians! West Virginia culture taking over!

and... Let's Gooooooooo Mountaineers!

I was searching for a recipe similar to the pepperoni rolls served on the Strip in Pittsburgh - the result of this recipe was pretty close. I followed the recipe as described. I used organic cane sugar which tends to be a little less sweet. Using my Kitchenaid mixer, I beat the eggs, added melted butter, then the yeast mixture and then added the flour mixture a little at a time, with the dough hook. There was about a 1/2 cup of flour that I did not use. I divided the dough into 4 large rolls because I wanted to cut and serve the rolls as an appetizer. Each roll had two rows of deli sliced pepperoni (overlapping) sprinkled with mozzarella cheese. Following the tips from another reviewer, I melted butter with pepperoni and brushed the tops with the pepperoni butter before placing the rolls in the oven. I baked the rolls on a parchment paper lined cookie sheet at 350 degrees for 25 minutes - until slightly brown on top. This was a good recipe - the pepperoni rolls were delicious. I will definitely use this recipe again.

Very good. Not quite what I used to get from a childhood bakery, but close. I would never go to the trouble to make cupcakes when I could just make a cake, so with this in mind I decided to make loaves instead of rolls. I made the dough in my bread maker. It's very sticky, so I removed it to waxed paper sprayed with Pam, and divided it into four sections. Rolled each section to about 9x12, put 40 pepperoni slices on each, and a handful of cheese. Baked for 35 minutes. The appearance of the second batch benefitted greatly from an egg wash, but next time I'll use butter as I think this must have been what that bakery used. Oh, and more cheese next time too. Thanks! I've been looking for a recipe like this for more years than I want to count. Beats the Rhodes bread dough recipe for sure!

I love this recipe for the dough. I use all ingredients as stated, but make on the dough setting of my bread machine. I then use the dough to make larger pepperoni bread loaves. It makes 3 HUGE or 4 average size loaves, approximately 14 inches long. I roll out the dough, spread with melted butter, sprinkle garlic powder, line with sliced provolone, and then use an entire pouch of Hormel sliced pepperoni between the loaves. Bake at 350 for approximately 30-40 min, depending on size of loaves. 
I think this is the only recipe for pepperoni bread dough that I have come across that gives the "defining taste" for pepperoni bread in SW Pennsylvania. Thank you so much for sharing kaoscarson!

Being from western PA this recipe is very similar to the local pep rolls at gas stations and such. Never had any issues with the dough. For the people who commented "it's dry" "biscuit like" or "didn't rise" they messed up. If the dough is dry and liquid, if it's wet add flour until you have the consistency you want. A little too much sugar for me I use 1/2C. After the dough rises at room temp I refrigerate until the next day. Much easier to work with. I roll these out this for each roll and add mozz cheese and sauce is also good. I make this at least twice a month for my kids lunches. They love them.

As a West Virginian this was really bad. The dough was difficult to work with, and the taste was way too sweet. A better way to make a good roll is to use a white bread recipe for the dough, take about 3 ounces of it, rolling it thinly, adding about 15 slices of pepperoni, and then rolling it up and tucking the sides in halfway through. Give it a good egg wash and brush with a mixture of olive oil and Italian seasoning for a roll that's way better. No offense to the author, but this recipe needs to be improved. I had intended to make lunch for someone really special to me using this recipe, but after tasting one of these rolls I’ve tossed all of them.

Yes!!! Use ALL the sugar! It’s how they are made in WV and Southwestern PA! I made them into smaller rolls. About 35-40 pepperoni rolls following the recipe as is. Just added a little garlic powder to the dough. When I assembled them I Added 3 pepperoni slices and shredded mozzarella cheese to every little one and pinched shut. Brushed with olive oil to bake 375 for 14 mins and once hot and out of the oven I brushed with melted butter.... mmmmm. So moist and flavorful with the cheese and pepperoni. Delicious and very much reminded me of the ones in Southwestern PA sold at the stores. I’m in NC now and love that I can make them like they do back up North! Great to freeze extras to use for making kids lunches too.

Good recipe! I am from WV and am no stranger to pepperoni rolls. We live in GA now and you can’t find pepperoni rolls around here so this recipe is much appreciated! I recommend letting the dough rise then punching it down and letting it rise again and punching it down again to get a less dense bread. Prefer to use Hudson Cream All Purpose flour for it. I’ve tried other flour brands and it just doesn’t work as well. I stuff mine with Hormel pepperoni slices and Sargento Shredded Provolone and Mozarella Cheese (and sometimes banana pepper rings) and serve it with Dei Fratelli pizza sauce to dip them in. If you don’t like a sweeter bread dough you can cut back on the sugar a little, but they won’t taste as authentic.

I used 8 slices of pepperoni in each and added pepper jack cheese in half the batch, the other batch I did the same but added jalapeno, delicious!! Note: add a thin slice of jalapeno to the top of the uncooked rolls so you can identify them after they've been baked.

I grew up in the Ohio Valley, very near to both WV and PA where these originated. Pepperoni rolls were a school lunch staple. I haven't had one in at least 15 years, but suddenly remembered them and wanted to make a batch for me and a friend.
I made some minor changes to this recipe, I used melted coconut oil in place of the butter and omitted the 3/4 cup sugar because a sweet dough didn't appeal to me. I also brushed the tops with melted butter and garlic salt both before and after baking. This recipe yielded 30 small rolls for me, and I did sprinkle some shredded mozzarella in half of them with the pepperoni. 16 mins at 350° was just right for these. They did not get browned, but were baked through and warm in the center. The dough was fluffy and soft and just perfect. These tasted exactly like I remember them.

I made this tonight for my husband. My mother in law is from WV, so he grew up eating homemade pepperoni rolls. I was a little nervous, but he loved them! His only request was to make it with a pepperoni stick rather than sliced pepperoni (that's how his aunt makes them.)I did make a few small changes based on other reviews. I cut the sugar to 2/3 cup. I baked for 14 minutes on 375 and once I removed the rolls from the oven I brushed with melted butter and sprinkled with Italian seasoning and sea salt. Instead of all purpose flour I used 3 cups of bread flour and 2 cups of wheat (I was all out of AP) My entire family enjoyed them and said to put these into the rotation!

We love these pepperoni rolls. I've made them many times. The dough is pretty easy to work with but I laugh at the amount of pepperoni it says to use. I use nearly triple the amount (I don't count usually) & a string cheese size amount of mozzarella as well. I don't get a many rolls but they're heartier.
I had to keep them in the oven for an additional five minutes. I also added mozzarella cheese. Awesome!
I added mozzarella cheese along with the pepperoni, as a personal preference. I also put some unsaltednstick butter on top of the rolls, they turned out fantastic!

Based on comments from others, I cut the sugar in half. I also added some mozzarella inside and a little extra pepperoni. These were very good. For my first attempt at making pepperoni rolls, these turned out much better than expected. The Man really liked them, and he's an extremely picky eater. I will be making more.
Delicious! Followed the recipe and "churched" it up a bit, with provolone cheese, topped it with Italian seasoning and fresh, grated parm. cheese. This West Virginia girl says YES to this recipe

I followed the recipe except for adding only 1/2 c sugar. I also baked them 15 minutes then basted on melted butter with a few sprinkles of garlic salt and dried parsley. Deeeeeelicious! Thanks for the recipe!

This was SO good AND easy! I was worried at the one hour mark, my dough wasn’t rising, but it finally doubled towards the end. I did add mozzarella cheese in the middle and Italian seasoning and garlic powder on top. Thank you so much for sharing this recipe.
Sprinkled some Italian seasoning, smeared on some butter and broiled them at the end to color the tops. They taste just like Mamaws who has lived in WV most of her life. Thank you for sharing!!
Great recipe. Dropped the sugar down to 1/4 cup due to personal preference. These are authentic to the WV classic recipe, and much better than buying prefab frozen dough as a lot of recipes suggest.
